summary:
This bill is an appropriations act for fiscal year 2025 (ending September 30, 2025) providing discretionary budget authority for the civil works of the Army Corps of Engineers, the Department of the Interior (Bureau of Reclamation and Central Utah Project), the Department of Energy (including atomic energy defense activities and power marketing administrations), and several independent agencies, while also enacting substantive legislative riders.

**Title I** appropriates funds for Corps of Engineers–Civil: Investigations ($159M), Construction ($3.01B, partially from the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund and Inland Waterways Trust Fund), Mississippi River and Tributaries ($370M), Operation and Maintenance ($5.714B, of which $3.106B derives from the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund), Regulatory Program ($218M, available through Sept. 30, 2026), FUSRAP ($200M), Flood Control and Coastal Emergencies ($45M), Expenses ($231M), and Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act administrative expenses ($5M). General provisions impose reprogramming constraints, require work plan adherence, and include policy riders such as prohibiting funds to alter eligibility under 33 U.S.C. § 701n (sec. 109), barring firearm restrictions at Corps projects (sec. 110), and prohibiting modification of certain nationwide permits (sec. 111).

**Title II** provides appropriations for the Central Utah Project Completion Account ($23M) and Bureau of Reclamation programs, including Water and Related Resources ($1.773B with transfer authority). General provisions extend sunset dates and increase authorization ceilings: e.g., the Calfed Bay-Delta Authorization Act’s authorization is extended to 2025 and its funding ceiling raised to $40M (sec. 203); the Reclamation States Emergency Drought Relief Act’s authorization is extended to 2025 and its ceiling raised to $130M (sec. 204). Section 206 mandates operation of the Central Valley Project and State Water Project in accordance with the 2019 Preferred Alternative and biological opinions. Section 209 amends the Water Infrastructure Improvements for the Nation Act (P.L. 114-322) to extend deadlines and increase authorizations, and raises ceilings for the Reclamation Wastewater and Groundwater Study (43 U.S.C. 390h) and the Water Desalination Act (42 U.S.C. 10301 note).

**Title III** appropriates funds for DOE Energy Programs (e.g., Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy $1.96B, Nuclear Energy $1.793B, Science $8.39B), atomic energy defense activities (Weapons Activities $20.338B, Defense Nuclear Nonproliferation $2.445B, Naval Reactors $2.118B, Defense Environmental Cleanup $7.132B), power marketing administrations, and FERC. General provisions include reprogramming and prior-notification requirements (sec. 301), a prohibition on Strategic Petroleum Reserve sales to entities owning ties to the Chinese Communist Party (sec. 308), and a bar on awards exceeding $10M to “entities of concern” as defined in P.L. 117-167 (sec. 309). Section 315 amends the Natural Gas Act (15 U.S.C. § 717b) to grant FERC exclusive authority to approve or deny LNG import/export facility siting and requires the Commission to deem such exportation or importation consistent with the public interest. Section 317 transfers $8.98B from unobligated IIJA and IRA balances to Nuclear Energy for advanced reactor deployment and demonstration projects and amends P.L. 117-169 to reduce corresponding authorizations.

**Title IV** appropriates funds for independent agencies, including the Nuclear Regulatory Commission ($955.4M, offset by fee collections), Appalachian Regional Commission ($200M), and Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board ($45M). General provisions require NRC compliance with 2011 internal procedures and establish reprogramming and reporting rules.

**Title V** contains government-wide general provisions, including a prohibition on using funds for finalizing certain energy conservation standards (sec. 514), a limitation on Columbia Basin Restoration Initiative funding to $300M (sec. 513), restrictions related to religious belief-based discrimination (sec. 507), and a spending reduction account of $0 (sec. 515). The short title is the “Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025.”
